claim_scope: Baiera genus-level fossil leaf specimen interpretation grounded in one museum CH106 outline, labelled Baiera asadai by the museum. Not a taxonomic redetermination, exact replica, whole plant or precise age/locality assertion. Museum Upper Jurassic/Jehol association is contradictory with modern Early Cretaceous Jehol literature and is explicitly not adopted. No Sphenobaiera or Baiera multipartita morphology substituted.

source_references.notes: Personally read museum label Baiera asadai Yabe et Oishi, Ginkgophyta, CH106 specimen photograph. Actual pixels show a narrow basal petiole opening into deeply separated flat long wedge/ribbon lobes, divided unevenly toward tips, preserved on gray slab. Chosen specimen only; no whole-tree features. Museum lists Upper Jurassic/Jehol/Liaoning and 11.5cm; PNAS2021 DOI10.1073/pnas.2107859118 abstract explicitly identifies Jehol as Early Cretaceous, so specimen age/locality is unresolved, not relabelled automatically. Wiley DOI10.1111/nph.20154 read only as comparison: Late Triassic B.multipartita is different material and not used for selected outline.

source_references.age_disagreement: Museum Upper Jurassic/Jehol label conflicts with Early Cretaceous Jehol literature. Exact specimen age remains unresolved; no precise age claimed.

source_references.rights_note: Original generated concept used as design guidance only; not a primary factual source or texture.
source_references.notes: CH106-like original silhouette uses one central basal wedge and unequal forked flat lobes. Fossil carbonized brown relief has finite thickness, not living green foliage. Original supporting shale slab, irregular nonrepeating edge. Petiole and lobe breadths accentuated gently for readability; no invented diagnostic venation or leaf-mining damage. Geometry meters are nominal teaching-prop scale, not a claim of scanned dimensions. Concept inspected: concept basal lobe blades are broader and more decorative than CH106; correct geometry to narrower flat strips and deeper uneven divisions, avoid transferring concept broad fan into fossil claim. Preserve seven-ish terminal tips, not exact division count.
